content.content: When a recording would land a draft whose recorded base no longer matches the owned set, the deccy CLI shall refuse, place nothing, and name each stale draft by its handle and the differing paths.
content.rationale:
The requirement is one sentence about the landing that a stale draft must not get, and every clause in it is a side a prerequisite has already fixed. The trigger takes both of its terms from qrqsxyzz as that node settles them: a draft's record carries a content-identity base, a draft is stale when that base no longer matches the owned set, and the comparison that discovers this is made at the recording. The sentence therefore says "a recording" and not a verb, a flag or a stage: qrqsxyzz places the comparison at the recording and leaves the rest of the timing open — eager against one path at a time, and where between reading the argument surface and writing anything the read is taken — so naming the moment of comparison here would be this requirement choosing among answers its parent declined to choose. The same clause says "would land a draft" because landing is the recording: rvyrosmp settles that `record <path>... --to <id>` is what places named edits into a named node's change, so a recording is the only thing that can land a draft and is the only place a refusal can stand in front of a landing. vkkwusty bounds which drafts that phrase reaches: a record is `open` or `landed`, the only transition is `open` to `landed` and it happens when the draft lands, so the draft a recording would land is one whose record is still open and no landed record is a draft still to be landed. The clause thus guards the landing of an open draft and nothing else; it does not reopen, re-check or re-state anything about a record that has landed.

The refusal is qrqsxyzz's answer to a base that no longer matches, stated as the requirement's main verb rather than as a new rule: a stale draft refuses landing. What the refusal is a refusal of comes from rvyrosmp — recording is placement-only, and `--to` still names the one change the edits would have entered — so "refuse" here means the placement does not happen rather than that it happens elsewhere, and the requirement names no alternative destination because its parent gives the recording none. "Place nothing" is the same fact read at the files and the graph: because rvyrosmp makes recording the placement and nothing more, a refused recording moves no named edit into any change, creates no node, and, as qrqsxyzz adds, moves no record's state and writes nothing of the graph. The sentence says nothing about how the refusal is delivered, and that is deliberate: qrqsxyzz leaves the refusal's wording, separators, ordering, stream and exit status unfixed, and rvyrosmp leaves the recording's answer to a refusal unfixed, so a requirement that fixed any of them would be settling what its prerequisites explicitly left to someone else.

Naming is where the fourth prerequisite enters. "Each stale draft by its handle" is owyntkvw read onto the refusal: the handle is the record's identity, minted for the draft and written into the record as its key, so a draft named in a refusal is named by that handle and by nothing else a record carries — a node id, an edit, a workspace path, or a change id would each name something other than the draft, and the parent says so. "Each" is the many-ness owyntkvw already allows and qrqsxyzz already carries into the refusal: one node may be named by several records at once — competitors within an edit or a redraft while an earlier draft is open — and the rule holds for each of them, so the refusal reports every stale record that the recording could have landed, once per record and by that record's handle. "The differing paths" takes its sense from qrqsxyzz too: the differences are computed path by path over the owned set, the base's entries and the owned content that no longer agree, so the paths named are that record's differing paths and not the paths the call happened to name, and a path outside the owned set is not among them. The requirement therefore says which paths are named and not how they are computed, listed or formatted, because the encoding of the base, the order of the paths and the shape of the message are all things qrqsxyzz leaves open.

Nothing here adds a commitment the four prerequisites do not carry. The requirement does not say what a stale draft may do afterwards, does not say the base is rewritten, cleared or re-taken, does not say which record wins when several are stale beyond naming each of them, and does not fix a retry, a repair or a second verb; those are the repair and lifetime questions qrqsxyzz, rvyrosmp, vkkwusty and owyntkvw each leave elsewhere, and the sentence stops at refusing, placing nothing, and naming. It is a requirement and not a description of code, so it also carries no claim about where in the implementation the comparison or the message sits. Read clause by clause, the refusal's occasion is qrqsxyzz with the recording named by rvyrosmp and the open draft bounded by vkkwusty, the refusal and its placing nothing are qrqsxyzz and rvyrosmp, and the naming of each stale draft by handle and differing paths is owyntkvw and qrqsxyzz together.
